note: Matches Beth’s posted transcription of 12 Oct (P045) word for word except “moved in on Oct. 11,” where her post drops “on.” Bracketed tags are editorial, not Wynona’s.

entries.label: 12 Oct 1890, continued
entries.text: … to keep. To-day has been dull and rainy, the leaves falling, covering the ground, as a reminder that winter is approaching. All hail! To Autumn, in which there is something so expressive to me. Uncle, Aunt [Thomas and Lib Hambleton] and I, home all day, till evening I came down to Uncle Will’s [William L. Shoemaker]. Had a dark and rainy drive, but not a lonesome one. This evening the first I spent in their new house. They moved in on Oct. 11. As far as a nice home goes, they have every advantage.

entries.label: Oct. 13.
entries.text: Nothing particular happened to-day. Had my regular school duties to attend to. Learned this wk. of {Groff’s} Mill being burned on Oct. 8, about 8 P.M. Much damage done. To-day is still dull, and very cold and raw air.

entries.label: Oct. 14.
entries.text: Just came home from school. Cleared about noon to-day, with wind in West, having a clear, bracing feeling in the air. The new book-case arrived at the school-house. Cost $6.00. To-day finished my second month of school. Last eve Neal & Sallie Hambleton made a call.

entries.label: Oct. 15.
entries.text: After I came home from school went up to Uncle Jacob’s, and spent about 1 hr. talking with Aunt Sallie and Mamie. Had a pleasant day at school. First load of coal hauled for winter. Weather is very clear and cool, drying up mud very fast.
